source_report: ICAR Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR) Guidelines
content: Cotton requires warm, sunny climate (25°C - 35°C). High rainfall at square formation and boll development causes square shedding and boll rotting. Warm humid weather (>70% RH, 28°C-32°C) triggers Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella) and Whitefly outbreaks. Spraying conditions: Wind speed must be 5-15 km/h; avoid spraying if rain is forecast within 6 hours. Withhold irrigation when topsoil moisture is sufficient and rain is expected.

Paddy thrives in mean temperatures of 22°C - 32°C with high humidity. Persistent cloudy conditions and relative humidity above 85% with dew trigger Pyricularia oryzae (Blast) and Brown Planthopper (BPH). Maintain 2-5 cm water level in field during panicle initiation, but drain field before heavy downpours (>50mm) to prevent submersion lodging. Apply Tricyclazole or Hexaconazole during clear sky windows.

Wheat requires cool vegetative periods (15°C - 20°C). Maximum temperature exceeding 30°C during grain filling (milking/dough stages) induces terminal heat stress, reducing thousand-grain weight. Provide light and frequent irrigation during evening hours when maximum temperature exceeds 30°C. Spray Potassium Nitrate (1%) to mitigate thermal shock.
